transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
President Trump is brushing off criticism for calling Russian leader Vladimir Putin his friend
when the two met last week with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
>> We want to make a deal.
We want to stop killing.
I could say he's not a friend.
I want to make a deal.
I got to get a deal done.
>> Trump took questions from reporters after speaking with service members from his Barilago estate in South Florida.
In an interview with the BBC, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the Trump administration is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks.
And that delays in delivering anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives.
He also said it was strange that Trump called Putin my friend in a picture of the two he posted.
Federal scientists are testing the air, soil and water in eastern Iowa for lead contamination
following Wendy's detonation of thousands of pounds of the bomb-making material lead azide.
The Army says it was unstable and a controlled explosion was the only way to get rid of it.
Eliza Billingham is with Iowa Public Radio.
>> The EPA says it has about 300 people sampling the air, ground and nearby surface water for lead contamination.
Lead is dangerous because it's a neurotoxin.
It's especially dangerous to children and people who are pregnant because of how it can inhibit childhood development.
The EPA has set legal limits for how much lead can be on window sills and floors of houses, for example.
So it and the Army are watching for lead levels on surfaces noted at Nation Zone to see if they exceed those limits.
But so far the EPA says its measurements haven't shown any lead dust.
>> The EPA says it took more than 1,500 samples of air, water and soil and dust before the detonation and hundreds after it.
And that results could come as soon as Friday.
Judges in Israel calling to drop some of the corruption charges against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The trial against him has been going on for six years.
Netanyahu denies wrongdoing.
NPR's Daniel Estrin reports from Tel Aviv.
In a surprise move, the judges overseeing Netanyahu's corruption trial called on Israel's attorney general to consider dropping the most serious case of bribery,
where Netanyahu was accused of trading business favors with a media mogul in exchange for positive news coverage.
In the second case involving Netanyahu's dealings with a newspaper owner, the judges said they doubted a crime was committed.
And the judges recommended the sides settle the final case, where Netanyahu is accused of getting gifts from a Hollywood producer and helping him with an Israeli tax break.
This is promising news for Netanyahu, but he may be unseated as Prime Minister as early as next week.
His rival, Gadi Eisenkot, is trying to form a new government.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
This is NPR News. China, Japan, and other U.S. trading partners are pushing back against President Trump's new tariff plan.
The new tariffs were announced Wednesday following a Section 301 investigation on excess capacity and production.
U.S. Trade Representative James Ingreer says the 14 economies has what he said are unreasonable practices regarding excess capacity.
China calls that a false premise, and Japan is also protesting.
U.S. Postal Service proposing more shipping price hikes to address its financial challenges.
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports that USPS has already paused at certain payments to retirement funds for postal workers.
Starting January 17th, shipping a package domestically with the U.S. Postal Service would cost about 6 percent more on average.
There would also be an 11 percent surcharge for rising fuel costs.
The Postal Regulatory Commission is now reviewing this proposal.
USPS says it's needed because the self-funded agency generally receives no tax dollars
and relies on stamp and service fees to deliver the mail at least six days a week to just about every address in the country.
Postmaster General David Steiner says USPS is coming up with new plans to avoid running out of cash in five years.
And I will present those plans to leadership throughout the government so that they can make the policy choice between reduced levels of service, a reform of our retirement plans, and funding the money-losing mandates.
In July, USPS raised the price of a first-class forever stamp to 82 cents. Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
Financial markets in Asia mostly higher, the head of Wall Street's reopening following the Thanksgiving Day holiday, benchmarks advancing in Tokyo, Sydney, Seoul, and Hong Kong.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.
prolonlife.com/npr.

Zelensky tells BBC Trump administration isn't pressing Russia hard enough in peace talks
EPA samples eastern Iowa air, soil, and water for lead after Army's azide detonation
Israeli judges urge dropping Netanyahu's most serious bribery charge, doubt another case
China, Japan push back against Trump's new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies
USPS proposes about 6% domestic shipping price hike plus 11% fuel surcharge starting January
Asian financial markets mostly rise as Wall Street reopens after Thanksgiving holiday
